      CITY OF RALEIGH HOUSING BONDS REFERENDUM
           Yes            Additional property taxes may be levied on property located in the City of Raleigh, North Carolina in an amount sufficient to pay the 
                          principal of and interest on bonds if approved by the following ballot question.
                          Shall the order adopted on May 19, 2026, authorizing not exceeding $101,500,000 HOUSING BONDS of the City of Raleigh, North 
                          Carolina, plus interest, for the purpose of providing funds, together with any other available funds, for community development 
                          programs to provide and rehabilitate multifamily and single family housing inside the corporate limits of said City, principally for the 
                          benefit of persons of low and moderate income, including, without limitation, (a) the construction or rehabilitation of housing or 
                          neighborhood revitalization improvements, (b) programs to provide loans and other financial assistance to such persons and to 
                          public and private providers of housing and (c) the acquisition of any related land, rights of way and equipment, and providing that 
                          additional taxes may be levied in an amount sufficient to pay the principal of and interest on the bonds, be approved, in light of the 
                          following:
                          (1) The estimated cumulative cost over the life of said bonds, using the highest interest rate charged for similar debt over the last 
                          20 years, would be $167,885,618, consisting of the $101,500,000 principal amount of said bonds, plus $66,385,618 of estimated 
                          interest.
                          (2) The estimated amount of property tax liability increase for each one hundred thousand dollars ($100,000) of property tax value 
                          to service the cumulative cost over the life of said bonds provided above would be $0 (zero dollars) per year.
           No             Additional property taxes may be levied on property located in the City of Raleigh, North Carolina in an amount sufficient to pay the 
                          principal of and interest on bonds if approved by the following ballot question.
                          Shall the order adopted on May 19, 2026, authorizing not exceeding $101,500,000 HOUSING BONDS of the City of Raleigh, North 
                          Carolina, plus interest, for the purpose of providing funds, together with any other available funds, for community development 
                          programs to provide and rehabilitate multifamily and single family housing inside the corporate limits of said City, principally for the 
                          benefit of persons of low and moderate income, including, without limitation, (a) the construction or rehabilitation of housing or 
                          neighborhood revitalization improvements, (b) programs to provide loans and other financial assistance to such persons and to 
                          public and private providers of housing and (c) the acquisition of any related land, rights of way and equipment, and providing that 
                          additional taxes may be levied in an amount sufficient to pay the principal of and interest on the bonds, be approved, in light of the 
                          following:
                          (1) The estimated cumulative cost over the life of said bonds, using the highest interest rate charged for similar debt over the last 
                          20 years, would be $167,885,618, consisting of the $101,500,000 principal amount of said bonds, plus $66,385,618 of estimated 
                          interest.
                          (2) The estimated amount of property tax liability increase for each one hundred thousand dollars ($100,000) of property tax value 
                          to service the cumulative cost over the life of said bonds provided above would be $0 (zero dollars) per year.

      TOWN OF KNIGHTDALE PARKS AND RECREATION BONDS REFERENDUM
           Yes            Additional property taxes may be levied on property located in the Town of Knightdale in an amount sufficient to pay the principal of 
                          and interest on bonds if approved by the following ballot question.
                          SHALL the order authorizing $55,000,000 of bonds plus interest to provide funds to pay the capital costs of designing, constructing, 
                          improving, and renovating Parks and Recreation facilities, including, but not limited to, the design and construction of a community 
                          center, improvements to existing park and recreation facilities, the acquisition and installation of furnishings and equipment related 
                          thereto, the acquisition of land, rights-of-way and easements in land required therefor, and related public infrastructure 
                          development, and providing that additional taxes may be levied in an amount sufficient to pay the principal of and interest on the 
                          bonds be approved, in light of the following:
                          (1) The estimated cumulative cost over the life of the bonds, using the highest interest rate charged for similar debt over the last 20 
                          years, would be $85,861,600 (consisting of $55,000,000 principal amount of the bonds plus $30,861,600 of interest).
                          (2) The estimated amount of property tax liability increase for each one hundred thousand dollars ($100,000) of property tax value 
                          to service the cumulative cost over the life of the bond provided above would be $35.00 per year.
           No             Additional property taxes may be levied on property located in the Town of Knightdale in an amount sufficient to pay the principal of 
                          and interest on bonds if approved by the following ballot question.

                          center, improvements to existing park and recreation facilities, the acquisition and installation of furnishings and equipment related 
                          thereto, the acquisition of land, rights-of-way and easements in land required therefor, and related public infrastructure 
                          development, and providing that additional taxes may be levied in an amount sufficient to pay the principal of and interest on the 
                          bonds be approved, in light of the following:
                          (1) The estimated cumulative cost over the life of the bonds, using the highest interest rate charged for similar debt over the last 20

                          (2) The estimated amount of property tax liability increase for each one hundred thousand dollars ($100,000) of property tax value 
                          to service the cumulative cost over the life of the bond provided above would be $35.00 per year.
      WAKE COUNTY SCHOOL BONDS REFERENDUM
           Yes            Additional property taxes may be levied on property located in the County of Wake, North Carolina in an amount sufficient to pay 
                          the principal and interest on school bonds if approved by the following ballot question.
                          Shall the order adopted on July 6, 2026, authorizing $680,000,000 SCHOOL BONDS of the County of Wake, North Carolina, plus 
                          interest, for the purpose of providing funds to construct, renovate, expand, improve and equip school buildings and other school 
                          facilities for the Wake County Public School System, and providing that additional taxes may be levied in an amount sufficient to 
                          pay the principal of and interest on said bonds be approved, in light of the following:
                          (1) The estimated cumulative cost over the life of said bonds, using the highest interest rate charged for similar debt over the last 
                          20 years, would be $1,043,387,458, consisting of the $680,000,000 principal amount of said bonds plus $363,387,458 of estimated 
                          interest.
                          (2) The estimated amount of property tax liability increase for each one hundred thousand dollars ($100,000) of property tax value 
                          to service the cumulative cost over the life of said bonds would be $4.10 per year.
           No             Additional property taxes may be levied on property located in the County of Wake, North Carolina in an amount sufficient to pay
